segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Jesus spoke to them again, saying,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Pharisees said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “You are testifying about yourself; your testimony is not true.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Even if I do testify about myself, my testimony is true, because I know where I came from and where I am going. But you do not know where I come from or where I am going.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You judge according to the flesh; I judge no one.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Yet even if I do judge, my judgment is true, because I am not alone; it is I and the Father who sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And in your own law it is written that the testimony of two people is true.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I am one who testifies about myself, and the Father who sent me testifies about me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Where is your father?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You know neither me nor my Father. If you knew me, you would know my Father also.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He spoke these words in the treasury, as he was teaching in the temple; and no one arrested him, because his hour had not yet come.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So he said to them again,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I am going away, and you will seek me, and you will die in your sin. Where I am going, you cannot come.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Jews said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Surely he is not going to kill himself, since he says, ‘Where I am going, you cannot come’?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You are from below; I am from above. You are from this world; I am not from this world.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: That is why I told you that you will die in your sins; for unless you believe that I am, you will die in your sins.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Who are you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Why am I speaking to you at all?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I have much to say about you and much to judge; but the one who sent me is true, and what I heard from him is what I speak to the world.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They did not understand that he was speaking to them about the Father.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am, and that I do nothing on my own, but speak these things just as the Father taught me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And the one who sent me is with me; he has not left me alone, because I always do what pleases him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As he was saying these things, many believed in him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus said to the Jews who had believed him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If you remain in my word, you are truly my disciples,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “We are Abraham’s offspring and have never been slaves to anyone. How can you say, ‘You will become free’?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly, truly, I tell you: everyone who commits sin is a slave of sin.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The slave does not remain in the household forever; the son remains forever.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So if the Son sets you free, you will really be free.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I know that you are Abraham’s offspring; yet you are seeking to kill me, because my word finds no room in you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I speak of what I have seen in the Father’s presence; and you, then, do what you have heard from your father.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Our father is Abraham.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If you are Abraham’s children, you would be doing the works of Abraham.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But now you are seeking to kill me, a man who has told you the truth that I heard from God. Abraham did not do this.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You are doing the works of your father.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “We were not born of sexual immorality; we have one Father, God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If God were your Father, you would love me, for I came from God and am here. I have not come on my own; he sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Why do you not understand the way I speak? Because you are unable to hear my word.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You are from your father, the devil, and you want to carry out your father’s desires. He was a murderer from the beginning and did not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks from what is his own, for he is a liar and the father of lies.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But because I tell the truth, you do not believe me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Which of you convicts me of sin? If I am telling the truth, why do you not believe me?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever is from God hears the words of God. This is why you do not hear: because you are not from God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The Jews answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Are we not right in saying that you are a Samaritan and have a demon?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I do not have a demon; rather, I honor my Father, and you dishonor me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But I do not seek my own glory; there is one who seeks it and judges.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly, truly, I tell you: whoever keeps my word will never see death.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The Jews said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Now we know that you have a demon. Abraham died, and so did the prophets, and yet you say, ‘Whoever keeps my word will never taste death.’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Surely you are not greater than our father Abraham, who died? The prophets died too. Who do you make yourself out to be?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing. It is my Father who glorifies me, the one of whom you say, ‘He is our God,’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: yet you have not come to know him. But I know him. If I were to say that I do not know him, I would be a liar like you. But I do know him, and I keep his word.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Abraham your father was overjoyed that he would see my day; he saw it and was glad.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the Jews said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “You are not yet fifty years old, and you have seen Abraham?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly, truly, I tell you: before Abraham came to be, I am.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they picked up stones to throw at him, but Jesus hid himself and went out of the temple.

notes.phrase: Then Jesus spoke to them again
notes.note: The SBLGNT text does not include John 7:53–8:11, the account of the woman caught in adultery, so this chapter begins at verse 12. The passage is missing from the earliest manuscripts and appears at different places in later ones. Most scholars regard it as an early tradition about Jesus that was not originally part of this Gospel. Without it, this scene continues the temple dispute of chapter 7.

The setting is still the Feast of Tabernacles (7:2, 37). The Mishnah describes great lamps being lit in the temple’s Court of Women during that festival, and many interpreters think Jesus’s claim plays on that ceremony, though the Gospel does not say so. Light was also an established scriptural image for God’s presence and guidance.

notes.phrase: the testimony of two people is true
notes.note: This summarizes rather than quotes the rule in Deuteronomy 17:6 and 19:15 that a matter must be established by two or three witnesses. Jesus names himself and the Father as the two. “True” here has the legal sense of valid or admissible, but the Greek word is the same one used for truth throughout the chapter, so it is kept.

This probably refers not to the storerooms themselves but to the part of the temple precincts where the offering chests stood, usually located in the Court of Women. It was a public and well-frequented place, which sharpens the remark that no one arrested him.

Jesus, his disciples and nearly everyone in this scene were Jews. In John the term often has a narrower reference: the Judean public in Jerusalem, and especially its religious authorities, in so far as they oppose Jesus. Some translators render it “Judeans” or “the Jewish leaders”. The traditional word is kept here, but it should not be read as a statement about the Jewish people as a whole.

The Greek is simply “I am” with nothing after it, here and in verses 28 and 58. Most English versions add “he” in verses 24 and 28, which is a legitimate reading since the phrase can mean “I am the one”. The bare form echoes God’s self-declaration in the Greek of Isaiah (for example 43:10, “that you may know and believe … that I am”). It is left unfilled so that the repetition, and the hearers’ puzzled “Who are you?”, come through.

notes.phrase: Why am I speaking to you at all?
notes.traditional: Just what I have been telling you from the beginning
notes.note: This is one of the most difficult sentences in the Gospel. The opening words can be an idiom meaning “at all”, giving an exasperated question, as the SBLGNT punctuates it and as several Greek-speaking early interpreters read it. They can also mean “from the beginning”, giving a statement: “What I have been telling you from the beginning.” Many English versions take the second option; the matter is unresolved.

The verb ordinarily means to raise high or to exalt. In John it carries a deliberate double sense: being raised up on the cross and being exalted (compare 3:14 and 12:32–33). English “lifted up” keeps both possibilities open.

The Greek says only “the father” in both halves of the verse; many manuscripts add “my” and “your”. The verb “do” can also be a command. The second half may therefore mean “so you too should do what you have heard from the Father”, as some versions have it. The rendering here takes it as a statement about a different father, which fits the reply in verse 39 and the charge in verses 41 and 44.

The Greek word covers unlawful sexual relations generally. The speakers may be insisting on their legitimate descent from Abraham. Because the prophets used the same word for Israel’s unfaithfulness to God (Hosea speaks of “children of immorality”), they may instead be denying idolatry, which suits their next words, “we have one Father, God”. Some interpreters also hear an insinuation about Jesus’s own birth, but this is uncertain.

Literally “a liar and the father of it” (or “of him”). The pronoun most naturally refers back to “the lie” just mentioned, hence “father of lies”; it could also mean “father of the liar”. A grammatically possible reading, “his father also is a liar”, is rejected by nearly all interpreters.

notes.phrase: before Abraham came to be, I am
notes.note: The Greek uses two different verbs: one for coming into existence, said of Abraham, and the plain present “I am”, said of Jesus. The traditional “before Abraham was” hides that contrast. The absolute “I am” echoes God’s self-declarations in the Greek Scriptures. The attempt to stone him in the next verse shows the hearers took it as a claim that amounted to blasphemy.

candidates.reason: Recurs constantly in John and Acts, where translators divide between “Jews”, “Judeans” and “Jewish leaders”, and inconsistency would badly mislead readers.
Central across the whole New Testament, and “believe”, “trust” and “have faith” are all defensible, so one policy is needed, including for the constructions with “in” and with the plain dative.
A Johannine keyword (“abide”, “remain”, “stay”, “continue”) whose thematic links across John and 1 John vanish if the English varies.
Ranges from the body to humanity to human standards across John and Paul, and translators differ sharply over keeping “flesh” or paraphrasing.
Appears in the Gospels, Acts, Paul and Revelation with literal and figurative senses, and “fornication”, “sexual immorality” and “prostitution” are all in use.
